Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 5–6 day history of dry, continuous cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, transient diarrhea; no dyspnea, chest pain, or sputum production.  
- Past history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension.  
- Most consistent with an acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold / influenza-like illness or possible COVID-19).  
- Alternative considerations: early/atypical pneumonia, evolving viral bronchitis. ACE-inhibitor cough unlikely given acute systemic symptoms (DDx supported but low likelihood).  
- Advised rest, hydration, and regular paracetamol.  
- Safety-net advice: return if symptoms worsen, fever persists, or no improvement in 2–3 days; possible need for antibiotics if bacterial infection suspected.

Management Plan
-  management_plan_main_or_not_recorded  
  • Rest at home for 1–2 days; consider delaying return to work.  
  • Hydration and symptomatic relief with paracetamol.  
  • Monitor for worsening cough, fever, or breathing difficulty; seek review if occurs.  
  • Discussed alcohol reduction for cardiometabolic health.  
  • Follow-up appointment if no improvement within 3 days or sooner if deterioration.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold/influenza/COVID-19) – High likelihood: aligns with acute onset, cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, brief GI upset.  
2. Acute viral bronchitis / post-viral cough – Moderate likelihood: persistent dry cough following viral prodrome; early course.  
3. Community-acquired atypical pneumonia – Low–moderate likelihood: systemic symptoms with dry cough; diabetes is a risk factor but absence of focal chest findings lowers probability.
